mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to reduced discount rates for equity valuations. The relationship is negative: as FEDFUNDS decreases, returns increase.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals economic weakness, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as the market anticipates policy support.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 5.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL signals a 'transitory inflation' narrative, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as the market prices in a temporary inflation shock without aggressive rate hikes.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS <= 0.1% and CPIAUCSL > 270, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market recovery (HOUST above 1500), the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive as housing strength signals broader economic expansion.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1500, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index 2017=100) signals a contraction in the real economy, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as the market anticipates policy support.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor force (PAYEMS) is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as stronger labor market conditions support consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The positive correlation between PAYEMS and 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts (HOUST) and rising residential fixed investment (RSAFS) signals a strong housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as the housing sector is a leading indicator of economic expansion.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1500 and RSAFS > 600000, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 270), the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative as the market prices in the risk of aggressive monetary policy tightening.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 270, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such periods.
